text:
marta: Heads up @ryan @ciara — raven-int8 canary shows ~2.7% funcall/schema failures vs fp16 ~0.4%. Failures look like malformed JSON (missing commas/quotes, stray colons) not just truncation. Any ideas?
ryan: Seen that on dedicated canary this morning. Correlation with KV-cache ON and sequence length spikes. Pushing a dump to /tmp/canary-dumps/2091122334.tar.gz.
ciara: Can you paste an example?
ryan: Sure — clean expected:
```json
{"tool":"search","args":{"query":"error handling","top_k":5}}
```
but model sometimes emits:
```json
{"tool":"search","args": "query: error handling, top_k:5"}
```
or
```json
{tool: "search", args: { query: "error handling" top_k:5 }}
```
marta: Those second forms are the worst — JS parse fails. They look like tokenization/spacing issues introduced post-quantization.
samir: Quick theory: int8 slightly shifts token probabilities so punctuation around keys becomes optional in generated text. Combined with truncated prefixes from KV cache we get non-compliant outputs.
ciara: Short-term mitigation: soft-schema-adapter in postprocess that does fuzzy repair + strict validation before handing off to tools. We prototyped a tiny healer that does: 1) convert single quotes -> double, 2) insert missing commas between key-value pairs, 3) wrap unquoted keys in quotes, 4) attempt to parse with relaxed JSON parser, 5) if still failing, run 1 retry of model with "fix JSON" prompt.
marta: Do we have numbers for that?
eval-bot: eval run summary (5k samples, question->toolcall set):
- int8 baseline parse_fail_rate: 2.68%
- int8 + soft-schema-adapter: 0.79%
- int8 + 1 retry (model) w/ adapter: 0.65%
- fp16 baseline parse_fail_rate: 0.36%
- p95 latency: int8 baseline 210ms, +adapter negligible (~+5ms), +retry +80ms (p95 = 290ms)
ciara: So adapter buys most of the wins with tiny latency hit. Retry helps but costs p95.
ryan: We need to watch false-healing: adapter might change intended structure (e.g., convert free text into object). Any examples?
eval-bot: False-heal check: on 5k corpus adapter introduced semantic changes in 0.04% of cases (detected by rerun evals comparing tool outputs).
samir: For production, propose layered policy: 1) try soft-schema-adapter, 2) if adapter fails or ambiguous, attempt 1 in-protocol retry, 3) fallback to a safe default response (error + human-in-the-loop) for paid enterprise routes.
marta: Agreed. Also add a canary variant that enables adapter only for int8 to measure user-impact metrics (latency, error, rerank quality).
ciara: Quick patch for adapter (JS):
```js
function softHeal(s) {
  s = s.replace(/'/g, '"'); // single -> double
  s = s.replace(/([a-zA-Z0-9_]+)\s*:\s*([\"\{\[])/g, '"$1": $2'); // unquoted keys
  s = s.replace(/\"\s*([\}\]])/g, '"$1'); // minor spacing fixes
  // try relaxed parse
  try { return JSON.parse(s); } catch(e) {}
  // try inserting commas between string/brace boundaries
  s = s.replace(/([\"\}\]])\s*([\"\{])/g, '$1, $2');
  try { return JSON.parse(s); } catch(e) { return null; }
}
```
samir: That looks fine for heuristic healing. We should open-source a more robust variant in devex repo.
marta: Action items: @ryan run int8-canary with adapter-only and collect p50/p95 and parse_fail_rate (assign to you). @ciara add unit fuzz tests that inject common punctuation drops and measure healing precision/recall (assign to you). @samir can you draft canary rollout policy with retry budget/latency guardrails?
samir: On it. Will draft today.
deploy-bot: Canary created: canary/int8-soft-adapter-2091122334 at 2091122380 — monitor dashboard: /canaries/2091122334
ryan: I'll grab the dashboards and post a quick heatmap after the first 2k requests.
ciara: If adapter stabilizes parse failures <1% we can keep it as default for int8 until model fix. Long term: also explore constrained decoding + stricter function-call schemas.
marta: Yep. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
